novelty_flags.one_line: The flagship reduction only postulates a generic map T and its desired properties; it supplies neither an explicit graph transformation nor a worked nondegenerate donor-to-DTE-conflict instance, so the claimed flagship construction is not yet exhibited.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:computational-hardness; prop:numerical-value-hardness; thm:frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The hardness statements are conditional on the Unique Games Conjecture and NP not being contained in BPP.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The certificate-aware and one-sided numerical frontiers are claimed only under UGC and NP not contained in BPP.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 24, 36--41, 86--87; Conjecture 2, Proposition 2.2, Appendix A.5, Lemma E.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Conjecture 2 asks for d^(1/2-epsilon) multiplicative hardness for regular-graph DTE minimax risk; Proposition 2.2 represents unrestricted ANI minimax risk by a conflict-graph function, and Appendix A.5 gives the maximal-independent-set reduction.
CGD samples desired-exposure variables, Proposition 3.5 proves modified Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness under ANI, and Theorem 4.1 gives its finite-sample spectral variance bound.
The paper proves UGC hardness for bounded-degree independent set within O(d/log^2 d) and obtains maximum degree through sparsification and deletion, rather than exact regularity.
The work develops graph-product hardness for induced and semi-induced matching; it does not itself state a DTE statistical-risk calibration.
